item.title: Sqwod Daily · Friday, 13 November 2026
item.description: Men now make up roughly a third of Pilates participants, reshaping studio demand, while the HFA named a permanent CEO and a new platform launched to connect studios with brand partners.
item.content:encoded:
Friday, 13 November 2026 View online →
DAILY
Friday, 13 November 2026 · Weekday
Men now a third of Pilates participants, HFA names permanent CEO & PIRL launches studio brand-deal platform
Your edge in the fitness industry. Five minutes, every weekday.
Men now make up roughly a third of Pilates participants, reshaping studio demand, while the HFA named a permanent CEO and a new platform launched to connect studios with brand partners.
Sqwod
 
5 jobs this week

See all jobs →
 
Connect the dots
Men are now a third of Pilates participants: what it means for studios
Men now account for roughly one third of Pilates participants, a marked shift in a category that was once dominated by women. Studios including Club Pilates, STRONG Pilates, and solidcore are responding by aligning their programming and messaging to reach both men and women. Industry observers describe this as a structural change in who is walking through the door, not a short-term spike.
For studio operators, a broader co-ed audience affects class design, marketing language, and potentially pricing and scheduling decisions. Studios that have not yet reviewed their messaging and programming mix for gender inclusivity have a concrete reason to do so now.
 
The rundown
01
Men now make up a third of Pilates participants, reshaping studio demand
Men account for roughly one third of Pilates participants, a marked shift in a category that was once dominated by women. Studios including Club Pilates, STRONG Pilates, and solidcore are responding to growing co-ed demand by aligning programming and messaging to reach both men and women. For studio operators, the broader audience represents a structural change in who is walking through the door, not a short-term spike.
Source: Fitt Insider →
02
WHOOP launches in-app social network for health and activity data
WHOOP launched WHOOP Humans, an in-app social network allowing its 3 million members to add friends, share Sleep, Recovery, and Strain scores, upload activities with photos, and comment on posts. The company says 57 percent of its members already belong to at least one Team, and members open the app eight times per day. For fitness platforms and brands, the move signals that keeping social activity inside a wearable ecosystem, rather than ceding it to Strava and its 200 million-plus users, is becoming a direct competitive priority.
Source: Fitt Insider →
03
HFA Names Greta Wagner Permanent President and CEO, Unveils Three-Year Plan
The Health & Fitness Association named Greta Wagner its permanent president and CEO on November 12 at Beyond Activ Americas in Dallas, after she spent six months in an interim role. Wagner led development of a three-year strategic plan, created with the HFA Board of Directors and industry stakeholders, aimed at delivering greater member value, strengthening advocacy, and expanding the industry's influence. For studio and gym operators who rely on HFA for lobbying and resources, the plan signals a more focused effort to make the association a stronger advocate for the industry.
Source: Health & Fitness Association →
04
Former Barry's and Grüns Execs Launch Studio Brand-Deal Platform PIRL
Ali Kaltman, formerly head of partnerships at Grüns, and Daniel Rabinovich, formerly VP of brand partnerships at Barry's, co-founded and launched PIRL on November 9, 2026. The platform matches brands with studios based on fitness discipline, member demographics, and geographic market, handles contracting and payments, and already counts Pvolve, SoulCycle, and Strong Pilates among its studio partners. Studios list for free; PIRL charges a fee on the brand side and holds funds until class attendance is verified before releasing payouts, giving studio operators a no-cost way to access brand revenue with a built-in attendance check.
Source: Athletech News →
05
Gantner launches face-recognition access system GT7 powered by XS4 Face
Gantner, an access control technology company, has released the GT7 powered by XS4 Face, a facial recognition system designed for fitness studios and health practices. The system identifies members with a brief look at a camera, requiring no card, smartphone or wristband, and is built to meet data protection and security standards. For studio operators, the technology can reduce front-desk workload, ease peak-hour congestion and support unstaffed or low-staff 24-hour access models.
Source: fitness MANAGEMENT →
 
Policy watch
HFA names Greta Wagner permanent president and CEO, launches three-year plan
The Health and Fitness Association named Greta Wagner its permanent president and chief executive on November 12, 2026, after six months in an interim role. Wagner led development of a three-year strategic plan, created with the HFA board and industry stakeholders, focused on member value, advocacy, and expanding the industry's influence.

The figure shows that social and competitive features inside wearable apps already have strong adoption, which matters for fitness platforms and studio operators deciding whether to integrate with or compete against wearable ecosystems.

item.title: Sqwod Daily · Thursday, 12 November 2026
item.description: Andrew Huberman is joining Hims & Hers as a board member in a deal worth up to $24M, as studio operators enter the fitness competition space and Groe Solutions adds commercial leadership.
item.content:encoded:
Thursday, 12 November 2026 View online →
DAILY
Thursday, 12 November 2026 · Weekday
Huberman joins Hims & Hers for up to $24M, studios launch fitness competitions & Groe names CCO
Your edge in the fitness industry. Five minutes, every weekday.
Andrew Huberman is joining Hims & Hers as a board member in a deal worth up to $24M, as studio operators enter the fitness competition space and Groe Solutions adds commercial leadership.
Sqwod
 
The rundown
01
Fitstop, Alpha Fit Club and F45 move into fitness competitions
Studio operators Fitstop, Alpha Fit Club and F45 are launching their own fitness competitions, entering a space where Hyrox has built significant consumer interest. Whether these operator-led formats can sustain themselves alongside Hyrox remains an open question for the sector.
Source: Athletech News →
02
Groe Solutions names Julio Marshall as Chief Commercial Officer
Groe Solutions announced that Julio Marshall has joined the company as chief commercial officer, a role in which he will lead commercial strategy, enterprise sales, revenue operations and strategic partnerships. Groe builds a gym intelligence platform that uses computer vision and management system integrations to combine member activity, facility demand and operational data in one view for multi-location health club operators. The appointment signals that Groe is pushing to connect that platform to senior decision makers across the industry.
Source: Club Solutions →
03
Swiss Re chief medical officer calls on insurers to invest in prevention
John Schoonbee, global chief medical officer of Swiss Re (Swiss Reinsurance Group), called on insurers to take a more active role in preventing ill health, citing worsening metabolic health and slowing mortality improvements as drivers of an unsustainable model. The call was reported by Health Club Management. For fitness operators, this signals that large reinsurance capital may be looking more seriously at prevention as a core business concern, not a peripheral one.
Source: Health Club Management →
04
Huberman joins Hims & Hers board in a deal worth up to $24M
Andrew Huberman is joining Hims & Hers as a non-independent board member, focused on science and marketing. Per a Securities and Exchange Commission filing, the deal includes $7M for two years of advisory work, $15M paid to Scicomm Media for three years of podcast advertising, up to $1M annually for optional short-form videos, and $50K cash plus $250K equity per year in board compensation. Hims is preparing to roll out sermorelin, glutathione, B12, NAD+, and L-carnitine, with BPC-157 and TB-500 to follow, signaling that brands are moving to position peptides as mainstream health products rather than niche biohacking tools.
Source: Fitt Insider →
05
JETSET Pilates uses AXLE platform to manage marketing across 150+ locations
JETSET Pilates has adopted AXLE, a technology platform serving fitness, wellness and beauty businesses, to coordinate marketing across its network of more than 150 franchise locations. The arrangement aims to give franchisees enough flexibility to run their own operations while keeping brand materials and campaigns consistent across the network. For multi-site franchise operators, the case points to the growing role of purpose-built technology in preventing brand misalignment as networks scale.
Source: Athletech News →
 
Policy watch
Swiss Re's top doctor calls on insurers to fund prevention
John Schoonbee, global chief medical officer of Swiss Re, the Swiss reinsurance group, called on insurers to take a more active role in preventing ill health, arguing that worsening metabolic health and slowing mortality improvements make the current model unsustainable. For fitness operators, this is a signal that large reinsurance capital may begin treating prevention as a core business concern, which could open new conversations around insurance-funded wellness partnerships.
 
Stat
150+
JETSET Pilates franchise locations managed through the AXLE marketing platform
At that scale, inconsistent brand execution across locations becomes a real operational risk, which is why purpose-built franchise marketing tools are attracting attention from growing networks.

item.description: Harvey Spevak, chairman of Equinox Group, organised a $6.5M round for longevity platform Vesalius; a London smoothie chain and a new premium gym also raised or launched this week.

DAILY
Wednesday, 11 November 2026 · Weekday
Vesalius Longevity Labs raises $6.5M backed by Equinox chair, Elevate smoothie bar raises $2.7M & Nord Gyms opens in London
Your edge in the fitness industry. Five minutes, every weekday.
Harvey Spevak, chairman of Equinox Group, organised a $6.5M round for longevity platform Vesalius; a London smoothie chain and a new premium gym also raised or launched this week.
Sqwod

Connect the dots
Equinox chair backs $6.5M raise for peptide and longevity platform
Vesalius Longevity Labs, a publicly traded company formerly known as Sweet Earth Holdings Corporation, completed a private placement of approximately 6.2 million units at $1.05 each, raising $6.5 million in gross proceeds. The investor group was organised by Harvey Spevak, chairman of Equinox Group. Vesalius connects licensed healthcare providers with peptide therapies and other longevity-focused services, and plans to use the funds to expand its sales team and enter new markets.
For studio and gym operators, the deal shows that capital from the top of the luxury fitness market is now flowing into provider-facing longevity platforms. That means operators who already serve health-conscious members may face new competition from medical providers offering longevity services, or find partnership opportunities with platforms like Vesalius.
 
The rundown
01
$6.5M Round for Vesalius Longevity Labs Led by Equinox Chair Harvey Spevak
Vesalius Longevity Labs, a publicly traded longevity company formerly known as Sweet Earth Holdings Corporation, raised $6.5 million through a private placement of approximately 6.2 million units at $1.05 each, with the investor group organised by Harvey Spevak, chairman of Equinox Group. The company plans to expand its sales team, enter new markets and grow its platform connecting licensed healthcare providers with peptide therapies and other longevity-focused services. Spevak's involvement signals that major luxury fitness operators are moving capital into provider-facing longevity platforms, a space studio and gym owners may increasingly compete with or partner alongside.
Source: Athletech News →
02
Nord Gyms to open first site in Crouch End, North London, in December
Nord Gyms will open its debut location in Crouch End, North London, in December, combining strength and conditioning facilities with personal coaching and contrast therapy. The concept pairs performance training with recovery in a single site, a format operators in the premium gym segment are increasingly testing.
Source: Health Club Management →
03
Gantner launches face recognition check-in system for fitness clubs
Gantner, an access and locker technology company, has introduced GT7 powered by XS4 Face, a facial recognition check-in system that identifies members via camera, checks their status in club management software in real time, and grants access without a card, smartphone or wristband. The system also supports RFID, QR codes and digital membership cards, and the company says the process complies with the DSGVO, the European Union data protection regulation. For studio operators running unstaffed or 24-hour facilities, automated face recognition check-in reduces reliance on front-desk staff and can help manage peak-time entry flows.
Source: body LIFE →
04
Elevate raises $2.7M to expand London smoothie bar chain
London-based smoothie bar Elevate secured $2.7M from JamJar Investments, Soho House founder Nick Jones, and others to open two new shops early next year. The brand already sells more than one smoothie per minute, posts over $1M in annual sales, and opened a second site inside Selfridges department store in April. Collaborations with Nike, SKIMS, and Adanola show how smoothie bars are building brand reach beyond food retail, a model studio and gym operators may find relevant as functional nutrition moves closer to their core offer.
Source: Fitt Insider →
 
Policy watch
Gantner face recognition system designed to meet EU data protection rules
Gantner says its GT7 powered by XS4 Face facial recognition check-in system complies with the DSGVO, the European Union data protection regulation that governs how personal and biometric data must be collected, stored and processed. Studio and gym operators in Europe considering biometric check-in should confirm any vendor's compliance documentation before deployment, as handling biometric data carries specific legal obligations under that regulation.
 
Stat
one smoothie per minute
Elevate's sales rate at the time of its funding round
Selling more than one smoothie per minute, alongside over $1 million in annual sales, gave Elevate the proof of demand needed to attract investors including JamJar Investments and Soho House founder Nick Jones.

DAILY
Tuesday, 10 November 2026 · Weekday
Virgin Active acquires Holmes Place Germany for €135m, DJs in gyms & Generation Ü fitness study
Your edge in the fitness industry. Five minutes, every weekday.
Virgin Active agreed to buy Holmes Place Germany for €135 million, marking its first major club acquisition and its entry into Europe's largest fitness market.
Sqwod
 
Money movement

The rundown
01
Virgin Active agrees €135m deal to acquire Holmes Place Germany
Virgin Active has signed an unconditional agreement to buy Holmes Place Germany for €135 million, giving it an immediate foothold in Europe's largest fitness market. The deal marks Virgin Active's first major acquisition of an established cluster of health clubs. For operators and investors watching international expansion, this signals that large-scale club acquisitions in Germany are live at nine-figure valuations.
Source: Health Club Management →
02
25.6% of 60-75 year-olds able and willing to keep working, study finds
A study on what researchers call 'Generation Ü', people aged 60 to 75, was presented at the Federal Press Conference in Berlin on 5 November 2026. It found that 71.3% of that age group have good physical fitness and a willingness to stay active, while 25.6% specifically want to remain in work and have the physical capacity to do so. The study concluded that targeted prevention programmes could enable more people in this age group to stay professionally active for longer, a direct signal for studio operators building services aimed at older adults.
Source: fitness MANAGEMENT →
03
Life Time and Basic-Fit bring DJs and dance floors into gyms
Gym operators including Life Time and Basic-Fit are adding DJ hires and dedicated dance floors to bring nightclub-style energy to workouts, according to Athletech News. Life Time has posted DJ job listings and Basic-Fit has introduced a gym dance floor as part of this shift. For operators, the moves signal that in-facility atmosphere is becoming a differentiator worth investing in.
Source: Athletech News →
04
Connected gym equipment market forecast to grow through 2035
IndexBox forecasts the global connected gym equipment market will expand through 2035, with commercial fitness centers driving demand by using connected equipment to improve member retention. For gym and studio operators, the forecast signals that investment in connected equipment is becoming a mainstream retention tool across the commercial sector.
Source: IndexBox →
 
Policy watch
German study links prevention programmes to longer working lives for over-60s
A study on what researchers call Generation Ü, people aged 60 to 75, was presented at the Federal Press Conference in Berlin on 5 November 2026. It found that 25.6 percent of that age group want to remain in work and have the physical capacity to do so, and that targeted prevention programmes could enable more people in this group to stay professionally active for longer.
 
Stat
71.3%
share of 60-to-75-year-olds with good physical fitness and willingness to stay active
The figure, from the Generation Ü study presented in Berlin on 5 November 2026, points to a large, underserved adult segment that studio operators building prevention or longevity programmes can target directly.

item.title: Sqwod Daily · Monday, 09 November 2026
item.description: Reborne Longevity has gone into administration, the HFA released a new foot-traffic tracker covering 11,000 US facilities, and WHOOP announced a retail deal with Ulta Beauty.
item.content:encoded:
Monday, 09 November 2026 View online →
DAILY
Monday, 09 November 2026 · Weekday
Reborne Longevity enters administration, HFA launches foot-traffic benchmark tool & WHOOP heads to Ulta Beauty
Your edge in the fitness industry. Five minutes, every weekday.
Reborne Longevity has gone into administration, the HFA released a new foot-traffic tracker covering 11,000 US facilities, and WHOOP announced a retail deal with Ulta Beauty.
Sqwod
 
Money movement
▼  Shutdown
Reborne Longevity
preventative health and recovery concept entered administration while building partnerships across fitness, wellness and healthcare
 
The rundown
01
Reborne Longevity enters administration
Reborne Longevity, a preventative health and recovery concept, has entered administration. The company was building partnerships across the fitness, wellness and healthcare sectors at the time of the shutdown. Operators and brands working with early-stage longevity concepts should note that partnership pipelines do not protect a business from insolvency.
Source: Health Club Management →
02
2026 NYC Marathon broke all records, Athletech News reports
The 2026 NYC Marathon broke all records, according to Athletech News, which published a report on the event on 6 November 2026. The source does not provide figures, participant numbers or further details beyond the record-breaking claim.
Source: Athletech News →
03
HFA launches FIT Tracker covering foot traffic at 11,000 US fitness facilities
The Health & Fitness Association released the Fitness Industry Traffic (FIT Tracker) on 5 November 2026, a quarterly report built on anonymized location data from nearly 11,000 gyms and studios across the United States. Developed with Sports Marketing Surveys USA, a Buffalo Groupe company, and powered by location analytics firm Placer.ai, it segments facilities into four categories: high-volume low-price gyms, mid-priced gyms, luxury clubs, and boutique studios, and also breaks results out by region. Operators and suppliers now have a benchmarking tool that shows how visit patterns shift across price points and geographies each quarter.
Source: Health & Fitness Association →
04
Garmin Exploring Waze Integration to Alert Drivers to Cyclists Nearby
Garmin is reportedly developing a feature that would send alerts to Waze drivers when a cyclist is ahead on the road, with evidence of the feature found in a Garmin Connect app update. The goal is to reduce crashes involving cyclists; IIHS data shows more than 1,000 cyclists were killed on roads between 2022 and 2024. Garmin already makes cycling computers, smartwatches with bicycle tracking, radar units and lights, signalling continued investment in cycling technology that coaches and fitness brands in the cycling category should track.
Source: autoevolution →
05
Gym cancels influencer's membership after 5-second machine stand
TikTok fitness creator Brandon (@bwrlifts) had his gym membership cancelled in early November 2026, three days after the gym owner sent him a message listing complaints that included a ban on "science-based lifting," a demand to stop grunting, and a complaint about stepping on leather equipment. The owner had also posted a screenshot from Brandon's workout video to the gym's own social media story. The dispute drew nearly 308,000 views on TikTok, a reminder that membership cancellations and owner-member disputes can become public events quickly when one party has an audience.
Source: Attack of the Fanboy →
06
WHOOP to sell fitness trackers at Ulta Beauty from March 2027
WHOOP announced on 3 November 2026 a retail partnership with Ulta Beauty to sell its WHOOP 5.0 and WHOOP MG devices, plus an exclusive range of bands and accessories, on Ulta.com and in select Ulta Beauty stores starting March 2027. The deal gives WHOOP access to Ulta Beauty's 47 million loyalty members and marks the wearable brand's first entry into specialty beauty retail. For fitness brands and studio operators, the move signals that health wearables are being positioned to reach wellness consumers through beauty retail channels, not just sports or technology stores.
Source: MobiHealthNews →
 
Stat
11,000
US gyms and studios tracked in the HFA FIT Tracker
Coverage across nearly 11,000 facilities makes this the broadest foot-traffic benchmark the US fitness industry has had, giving operators a meaningful sample to compare against their own visit data.

item.content:encoded:

DAILY
Sunday, 08 November 2026 · Weekday
Planet Fitness acquires Be-Fit for €102.5m, Keybanc raises PLNT target & GWI wellness economy hits US$7.5trn
Your edge in the fitness industry. Five minutes, every weekday.
Planet Fitness completed a €102.5m acquisition of Portuguese operator Be-Fit, adding 25 clubs and 80,000 members to its network.
Sqwod
 
Money movement
⇄  Acquired
Planet Fitness

▲  Valuation
Planet Fitness
Keybanc raised its price target to $68 from $65, maintaining an Overweight rating, implying 13.2% upside from the 5 November closing price of $60.07
 
Connect the dots
Planet Fitness buys Portugal's Be-Fit for €102.5m
Planet Fitness completed the acquisition of Be-Fit, a Portuguese gym operator, for €102.5 million. The deal adds 25 clubs and approximately 80,000 members to the Planet Fitness network, marking a significant entry into the Portuguese market.
For operators and investors watching European fitness, this deal is a signal that large chains are actively consolidating the region. If you run studios or clubs in markets where a major chain does not yet have scale, expect more acquisition approaches and more price competition as global operators look to grow quickly through purchase rather than new builds.
 
The rundown
01
Keybanc raises Planet Fitness price target to $68 from $65
Keybanc maintained its Overweight rating on Planet Fitness and raised its price target to $68 from $65, a 4.6% increase. The new target implies a 13.2% upside from the Planet Fitness closing price of $60.07 on 5 November. For investors and brands selling into the value gym segment, the upgrade signals continued analyst confidence in Planet Fitness as a growth stock.
Source: TradingView →
02
Planet Fitness completes €102.5m acquisition of Portugal's Be-Fit
Planet Fitness has acquired Portuguese gym operator Be-Fit for €102.5 million, adding 25 clubs and around 80,000 members to its network. The deal signals that Planet Fitness is expanding into the Portuguese market at scale, which operators and investors in European fitness should note as a sign of growing consolidation in the region.
Source: Health Club Management →
03
GWI: global wellness economy hit US$7.5trn in 2025, may reach US$10.9trn by 2030
The Global Wellness Institute released research on 11 November showing the global wellness economy reached a record US$7.5 trillion in 2025. The institute projects that figure will grow to US$10.9 trillion by 2030.
Source: Health Club Management →
 
Stat
US$7.5 trillion
Global wellness economy size in 2025, as reported by the Global Wellness Institute
The Global Wellness Institute projected this figure will grow to US$10.9 trillion by 2030, which points to sustained demand for fitness, health and related services over the next several years.

✓ Track: Monitor quarterly earnings calls and analyst notes for the large publicly listed gym chains in your region. These reports often signal where consolidation is heading and which markets are attracting capital, giving you time to position your business before competition increases.
✓ Try: Run a simple annual revenue-per-member calculation for your studio or gym and compare it across your membership tiers. Knowing this number helps you identify which products or services drive the most value and where to focus retention efforts.

Ausbildung Sport- und Fitnesskaufmann/-frau (m/w/d) (IST) at MEDA Sportakademie GmbH, Groß Nordende, €10,800–€13,200 / year
See all jobs →
 
Connect the dots
How HOTWORX built 913 locations by keeping operations simple
Stephen Smith, founder and CEO of HOTWORX, appeared on the Club Solutions podcast with editor Taylor Gabhart to explain the approach behind his infrared fitness franchise's growth to 913 locations. Smith credited a recurring monthly dues model, which he said has anchored fitness business models for more than 30 years by smoothing cash flow, and a philosophy he calls 'more workout, less time', which shortens session length to save members time and money. He described disciplined control of staffing, technology and programming complexity as the repeatable engine behind the brand's expansion, with 1,000 locations now in sight.
For operators and coaches weighing what to add, Smith's account is a direct argument that restricting complexity is itself a growth strategy. Keeping the member promise narrow and the labour model lean means each new location replicates the same proven system rather than inheriting the problems of a more elaborate operation.
 
The rundown
01
DSSV study finds wide variation in fitness potential among adults aged 60–75
The DSSV, Germany's association of fitness and health club operators, released a study on 5 November 2026 at the Federal Press Conference in Berlin examining adults aged 60 to 75, known as Generation Ü. The study found this age group holds significant potential for continued work and social participation, but that health, social connection, and individual motivation vary considerably within it. For studio operators and coaches, the findings point to the risk of treating older adults as a single segment and suggest that programming for this demographic needs to account for wide differences in capacity and motivation.
Source: DSSV →
02
HOTWORX CEO Stephen Smith outlines how simplicity drives 913-location growth
Stephen Smith, founder and CEO of HOTWORX, appeared on the Club Solutions podcast with editor Taylor Gabhart to explain how keeping operations simple, staffing lean and the member promise clear has driven the infrared fitness brand to 913 locations, with 1,000 in sight. Smith credited the recurring monthly dues model, which he said has anchored fitness business models for more than 30 years by smoothing cash flow, and a 'more workout, less time' philosophy that reduces session length to save members both time and money. For operators weighing how much technology and programming to add, Smith's account is a direct argument that restricting complexity is itself a growth strategy.
Source: Club Solutions →
03
Strong Pilates targets 20 new UK studios in 2027 after doubling its footprint in 2026
The Australian-born boutique fitness franchise opened seven UK studios in 2026, bringing its total to 15 locations, up from eight at the end of 2025. Confirmed sites include Nine Elms in early 2027, with franchisees exploring West Hampstead, St Albans, White City and Richmond. The pace of expansion signals strong franchisee demand in the UK market, particularly across London and the South East.
Source: Athletech News →
04
Punjab offers free online UPSC and PCS exam coaching to 1,000 students
The Punjab government announced free online coaching for the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) Civil Services Examination and Punjab Civil Services (PCS) examinations, targeting 1,000 college students across the state. Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann announced the initiative, with 750 of the 1,000 seats reserved. The programme is aimed at students from financially disadvantaged backgrounds.
Source: The Times of India →
05
fitness MANAGEMENT publishes new edition of medical fitness and healthcare
fitness MANAGEMENT released a new edition of its medical fitness and healthcare magazine, known as mfhc, on 6 November 2026. The mfhc is a twice-yearly specialist publication covering sports medicine, diabetology, rehabilitation, prevention and nutrition, distributed to fitness and health facilities in Germany, Austria and Switzerland, as well as industry companies, congresses and trade fairs. For operators and coaches working at the intersection of fitness and healthcare, the publication is a channel to stay current on clinical and preventive topics relevant to medically oriented facilities.
Source: fitness MANAGEMENT →
 
Policy watch
DSSV study: adults 60–75 vary widely in fitness capacity and motivation
The DSSV, Germany's association of fitness and health club operators, released a study on 5 November 2026 at the Federal Press Conference in Berlin showing that health, social connection and motivation differ considerably within the 60-to-75 age group. For studio operators and coaches, the findings point to the risk of treating older adults as a single segment and suggest that programming for this demographic needs to account for wide differences in capacity and motivation.
 
Stat
15
Strong Pilates UK studio locations as of late 2026, up from 8 at end of 2025
Strong Pilates nearly doubled its UK footprint in 2026 and is targeting 20 new studios there in 2027, signalling strong franchisee demand in London and the South East.

item.title: Sqwod Daily · Thursday, 05 November 2026
item.description: VersaClimber passed majority ownership to two of its own executives, while an Indian fitness aggregator closed its first funding round and Germany's annual fitness census opened for submissions.
item.content:encoded:
Thursday, 05 November 2026 View online →
DAILY
Thursday, 05 November 2026 · Weekday
VersaClimber ownership shifts to Schieffer & Siegrist, OBSESS raises $316K & DSSV launches 2027 German fitness survey
Your edge in the fitness industry. Five minutes, every weekday.
VersaClimber passed majority ownership to two of its own executives, while an Indian fitness aggregator closed its first funding round and Germany's annual fitness census opened for submissions.
Sqwod
 
Money movement
▲  Raise
OBSESS
 $316K

The rundown
01
VersaClimber executives Schieffer and Siegrist become majority owners
Shane Schieffer and Jim Siegrist, who have led strategy and sales at VersaClimber respectively, became majority owners of the Santa Ana, California-based equipment brand on 4 November 2026. Schieffer takes the role of chief executive and Siegrist becomes president and chief revenue officer, while the founding Charnitski family retains a minority stake after 45 years of ownership. Studio operators who stock or program VersaClimber equipment can expect continued investment in product development and partnerships, given Siegrist's existing relationships with brands such as Lagree Fitness and TRX.
Source: Health & Fitness Association →
02
DSSV launches 2027 German fitness industry data survey
The DSSV, Germany's association of fitness and health club operators, Deloitte, and the Deutsche Hochschule für Prävention und Gesundheitsmanagement (DHfPG), a German university specialising in prevention and health management, launched their annual data collection for the Eckdaten der deutschen Fitnesswirtschaft 2027 study on 4 November 2026, calling on all fitness and health facility operators in Germany to participate. The most recent figures show the German fitness sector recorded 12.36 million members, 9,647 facilities, and total revenue of 6.25 billion euros in 2025. Operators facing high running costs, staff shortages, and regulatory pressure stand to benefit from the benchmark data the study produces, which has tracked German market trends annually since 1989.
Source: DSSV →
03
OBSESS raises $316K angel round to connect India's fitness market
Noida-based fitness platform OBSESS closed an angel round of approximately Rs 3 crore ($316K) on 2 November 2026, about eight months after its March 2026 launch. The round was backed by Centricity co-founder Pushpendra Singh, Amit Goel, and Harshit Vij, with proceeds earmarked for partnerships, ecosystem expansion, and technology. OBSESS connects users with gyms, sports facilities, trainers, nutrition services, and fitness products on a single platform, signalling early investor appetite for aggregator models in India's fragmented fitness market.
Source: Dealroom →
 
Policy watch
DSSV opens 2027 German fitness industry data survey
On 4 November 2026, the DSSV, Germany's association of fitness and health club operators, Deloitte, and the DHfPG, a German university specialising in prevention and health management, launched data collection for their annual Eckdaten der deutschen Fitnesswirtschaft 2027 study, calling on all German fitness and health facility operators to submit data. The study has tracked German market conditions annually since 1989, and its benchmark figures help operators make decisions on costs, staffing and regulatory compliance.

total revenue of the German fitness sector in 2025
Germany's fitness and health club industry generated 6.25 billion euros in 2025 across 9,647 facilities and 12.36 million members, underscoring its scale even as operators contend with high running costs, staff shortages and regulatory pressure.

item.description: Arcana's new multi-studio membership hits New York City, Kimberly-Clark completes its Kenvue acquisition, and a London hotel integrates medical care with fitness.
item.content:encoded:
Wednesday, 04 November 2026 View online →
DAILY
Wednesday, 04 November 2026 · Weekday
Arcana launches NYC multi-studio membership at $325/month, Kimberly-Clark closes $48.7B Kenvue deal & St Clement hotel merges medical and fitness
Your edge in the fitness industry. Five minutes, every weekday.
Arcana's new multi-studio membership hits New York City, Kimberly-Clark completes its Kenvue acquisition, and a London hotel integrates medical care with fitness.
Sqwod
 
Money movement

Connect the dots
Arcana's multi-studio membership model launches in New York City
Arcana launched in New York City with more than 10 boutique studios on its network. Members pay $325 a month for nine classes plus wellness perks, booked through a single account. Partner studios include Reforming Pilates, The Training Lab, Nrthrn Strong, Sui Yoga, ID Hot Yoga, Güdsport, Nofar Method, The Silhouette Method, Good Day Pilates, Elahni, Serotonin Club, Powered on Bond, First Class Form and Outershed. Co-founders Felicia Dodge, who worked in analytics at Twitter and Visa and holds a master's in applied analytics from Columbia University, and Cole Tomlinson, a former mobile software engineer at Wayfair and Trello, started the company after working as yoga instructors and finding it difficult to train across multiple studios.
For studio operators, Arcana represents a multi-studio access product, similar to a network pass, that positions itself as protecting partner revenue rather than undercutting it. Studios already on the network gain exposure to members who might not have found them otherwise, while the $325 price point sits firmly in the premium tier, which may help avoid the margin pressure that lower-cost aggregators can create.
 
The rundown
01
Arcana Launches NYC Multi-Studio Membership Starting at $325 a Month
Arcana, a new premium fitness membership, launched in New York City with more than 10 boutique studios on its network, offering subscribers nine classes a month plus wellness perks from a single account. Co-founders Felicia Dodge, who brings a background in analytics at Twitter and Visa, and Cole Tomlinson, a former mobile software engineer at Wayfair and Trello, started the company after working as yoga instructors and finding it difficult to train across multiple studios. For studio operators, the model signals growing demand for multi-studio access products that aim to protect partner revenue rather than commoditise it.
Source: Athletech News →
02
Kimberly-Clark closes $48.7B Kenvue deal to build wellness portfolio
Kimberly-Clark completed its $48.7 billion cash-and-stock acquisition of Kenvue on 3 November 2026, uniting 10 billion-dollar brands across personal care, consumer health, women's health, and active aging. The combined company projects approximately $2.1 billion in run-rate synergies from cost savings and revenue growth. For brands and investors in the wellness and personal care space, the deal signals that large consumer goods companies are consolidating around health and wellness at scale, which may reshape supplier relationships and competitive dynamics for smaller operators in those categories.
Source: Personal Care Insights →
03
St Clement hotel in London combines medical, fitness and wellness under one roof
The Health Club at St Clement, the new London hotel from Soho House founder Nick Jones located at 180 The Thames, has launched with medical services, fitness and wellness integrated together, with Cleveland Clinic among its named collaborators. The pairing of a recognised medical institution with a hospitality-led fitness offer signals growing operator appetite for clinical credibility as a differentiator in the premium wellness market.
Source: Health Club Management →
 
Stat
$2.1 billion
projected run-rate synergies from the Kimberly-Clark and Kenvue combination
The scale of expected savings and revenue gains from this single deal illustrates how aggressively large consumer health companies are pursuing consolidation in the wellness space.

item.content:encoded:
Tuesday, 03 November 2026 View online →
DAILY
Tuesday, 03 November 2026 · Weekday
Equinox names Brendan Whitworth CEO with $1B growth plan & Mark Mastrov opens $10M Las Vegas club in 2027
Your edge in the fitness industry. Five minutes, every weekday.
Equinox has a new CEO and a $1 billion growth commitment, while 24 Hour Fitness founder Mark Mastrov is building a $10 million flagship club in Las Vegas.
Sqwod
 
Money movement
▲  Raise
Equinox
 $1B
planned growth investment announced alongside new CEO appointment
 
Connect the dots
Equinox installs new CEO and signals $1 billion in growth spending
Equinox appointed Brendan Whitworth as chief executive officer, replacing Harvey Spevak, who led the company since 1999 and moves to the chairman role. Whitworth joins from Anheuser-Busch, where he was also CEO, and will sit on the Equinox board. The company operates 118 clubs across 18 major markets and reported double-digit revenue growth, with membership numbers and check-ins at all-time highs. The transition comes as Equinox plans $1 billion in growth investment.
For studio and gym operators, the Equinox numbers confirm that premium, full-service clubs are still drawing members and capital. If your positioning competes on experience and results rather than price, the data supports holding that ground and investing in the quality signals that justify a premium membership fee.
 
The rundown
01
Equinox Names Brendan Whitworth CEO, Plans $1B in Growth Investment
Equinox appointed Brendan Whitworth as chief executive officer, replacing Harvey Spevak, who led the company since 1999 and moves to chairman. Whitworth joins from Anheuser-Busch, where he served as CEO, and will also sit on the Equinox board. The company reported double-digit revenue growth across its 118 clubs in 18 major markets, with membership numbers and check-ins at all-time highs, signalling that premium fitness continues to attract both capital and consumers.
Source: Club Solutions →
02
24 Hour Fitness founder opens $10M Founders Club in Las Vegas in early 2027
Mark Mastrov, who founded 24 Hour Fitness in 1983, will open Founders Club by 24 Hour Fitness in early 2027 at 9200 West Sahara Avenue in Summerlin, Las Vegas. The new facility covers more than 45,000 square feet and represents a $10 million investment, including more than $1 million in recovery equipment, with 25,000 square feet dedicated to free weights and strength training across 12 platforms. The scale of the recovery investment signals that operators building full-service clubs are treating recovery infrastructure as a core offering rather than an add-on.
Source: Club Solutions →
 
Stat

floor space dedicated to free weights and strength training at Founders Club by 24 Hour Fitness
Dedicating more than half of a 45,000-square-foot facility to free weights and strength across 12 platforms shows how central strength training has become to the full-service club offer.

Monday, 02 November 2026 View online →
DAILY
Monday, 02 November 2026 · Weekday
Fund 1 bids to take Xponential private, Whoop signs LeBron James & Chuze adds Reformer Pilates
Your edge in the fitness industry. Five minutes, every weekday.
Fund 1 Investments is exploring a bid to take Xponential Fitness private, while Whoop signs LeBron James and Chuze Fitness rolls out Reformer Pilates studios.
Sqwod
 
Money movement
⇄  Acquired
Fund 1 Investments LLC
third-largest Xponential Fitness shareholder is exploring a bid to take the company private
 
The rundown
01
Sekonda launches £79.99 subscription-free smart ring
British watch brand Sekonda expanded its wearable technology range with a smart ring priced at £79.99, requiring no ongoing subscription, to track health and wellbeing around the clock. The no-subscription model may be a useful talking point for operators and coaches recommending wearables to cost-conscious clients.
Source: Health Club Management →
02
Chuze Fitness adds Reformer Pilates studios for MAX members
Chuze Fitness launched Reformer Pilates studios in select locations, offering FreeMotion Reform RX-S reformers in purpose-built spaces with no per-class fees for MAX members. The hybrid model splits each studio between instructor-led group classes and self-guided sessions using on-demand video kiosks, backed by more than 300 iFIT-powered classes at beginner, intermediate and advanced levels. For operators considering Reformer Pilates, the model points to one way to address the instructor shortage and equipment intimidation that have kept the format out of mainstream gym environments.
Source: Club Solutions →
03
James Hird joins AI sports data firm backed by Paul Little
Essendon AFL football legend James Hird has put his coaching ambitions on hold to join an artificial intelligence software firm backed by billionaire Paul Little, which targets the commercial sports data market. Hird's move followed the appointment of former teammate Mark McVeigh as Essendon senior coach in August, after a public campaign to install Hird in that role did not succeed.
Source: AFR →
04
Whoop signs LeBron James as global ambassador with 3.5 million members
Health and fitness tracker Whoop signed NBA star LeBron James as its newest global ambassador, the company announced on 29 October 2026. James first wore a Whoop in 2015 as one of its first 100 members, and will now appear in multimedia ad campaigns for the brand, which has 3.5 million active paying members. For fitness brands and investors, the deal signals that wearable companies are investing in high-profile athlete partnerships as they build consumer scale ahead of a potential public offering.
Source: Sportico.com →
05
Fund 1 Investments Pushes to Take Xponential Fitness Private
Fund 1 Investments LLC, the third-largest shareholder in Xponential Fitness Inc., is seeking to take the company private and is exploring a bid to buy it outright, according to people familiar with the matter. Xponential Fitness owns the Club Pilates brand among other boutique fitness franchises. A successful take-private would remove Xponential from public markets, which could affect how its franchise partners, competitors and suppliers engage with the company going forward.
Source: Athletech News →
 
Stat

Whoop active paying members at the time of the LeBron James signing
The figure shows the scale Whoop has reached as a subscription wearable brand, providing context for why a high-profile ambassador deal with LeBron James makes commercial sense at this stage.

DAILY
Sunday, 01 November 2026 · Weekday
Founders Club launches as all-in-one training and medical wellness concept, Runna data shows 52% of Gen Z want to marathon but 7% act & Stryv raises $11.5M
Your edge in the fitness industry. Five minutes, every weekday.
Mark Mastrov launched Founders Club, a venue combining strength training, recovery, medical spa and social space, pointing to where premium fitness is heading.
Sqwod
 
Money movement

Stryv

The rundown
01
Kyle Scheele named second-day keynote speaker at HFA Show 2027
The Health and Fitness Association announced on October 30, 2026 that Kyle Scheele will deliver the second-day keynote, titled "Rethinking What's Possible," at The HFA Show 2027, running March 10–12 at Mandalay Bay in Las Vegas. Scheele, known for large-scale creative projects, will address how organisations can challenge conventional thinking and turn constraints into opportunities. The keynote is sponsored by Matrix Fitness.
Source: Health & Fitness Association →
02
Mark Mastrov unveils Founders Club, a fitness, recovery and medical spa concept
24 Hour Fitness founder Mark Mastrov has launched Founders Club, a new wellness concept that combines strength training, recovery facilities, a medical spa, and spaces for working and socialising. The concept signals operator interest in bundling training, recovery and medical wellness under one roof.
Source: Health Club Management →
03
Stryv raises US$11.5M Series B to push deeper into Asian wellness hardware
Singapore-based Stryv, a personal care and home wellness brand owned by Evo Commerce, closed an US$11.5 million Series B round on October 27, 2026, led by ACV Capital with participation from Openspace Capital and OCTAVE Capital. The company sells hair dryers, styling tools, massage chairs and air purifiers, and will use the funds to enter Taiwan and expand in Malaysia and Hong Kong, alongside research and development and potential acquisitions. The raise signals growing investor appetite for consumer wellness hardware in Southeast and East Asia, a category that increasingly overlaps with the recovery and self-care products fitness operators stock and recommend.
Source: Alvinology →
04
NYC Marathon valued at $339m as top races become major brands
The New York City Marathon carried a valuation of $339 million as of late October 2026, with major races in London, Paris and Chicago seeing similar increases in value. The figures signal that large running events have grown into significant commercial properties. For fitness brands and studio operators targeting runners, the scale of these events points to growing sponsorship and partnership opportunities in the running category.
Source: Athletech News →
05
52% of Gen Z want to run a marathon but only 7% commit, Runna data shows
New data from running app Runna, published October 30 2026, found nearly a third of Americans and 52% of Gen Z aspire to run a marathon, yet just 7% have committed to a race or physical challenge. Almost half of respondents said they do not consider themselves runners, and a third doubted their fitness level. Run club and event participation fell year on year as costs rose, a signal that operators and brands pricing or positioning running as exclusive risk shrinking the market they depend on.
Source: Fitt Insider →
 
Stat
7%
share of Americans who have committed to a race or physical challenge, per Runna data published October 30 2026
Despite 52% of Gen Z saying they want to run a marathon, only 7% have made a commitment, and run club participation fell year on year as costs rose, meaning studios and brands that lower the price and perceived barrier to entry have the largest addressable pool of new participants.
